global: Feasibility verdict: the plan is achievable only as a narrow slice. Realistic by 25 Nov: H1 and H3 pilot on D5 (if sign 10-11 Nov, review by 16 Nov), AA pilot descriptive fit (if rows verified 15 Nov), D4 demo, honest negative-results slides, 29-diag if Kush signs. The MUST list overstates scope: about 16 MUST items are agent-heavy side projects (lot-state build and matcher, MECH authoring and mechanism windows, Step 35, three dataset cards, three D5 run-alias items) that no headline result depends on; I demoted those. The real bottleneck is two humans: counting each alias once, each needs roughly 16-20 h between 9 and 16 Nov, and Kush's and Parv's other commitments in that week are unknown. The listing repeats the same human task (07.A labels, AA verification, D5 sign and review) across 5-6 topics with different hours, which inflates and confuses load; see missing item T9-C26-R3. Critical order: (1) Q39 and Step-35 decisions and the single pre-signature edit pass by 10 Nov (prereg is hash-bound, so every wording change including AC1 ruling, H3 reword, power note, embedding choice must precede the signature); (2) signatures and AA PDF downloads 10-11 Nov; (3) 07.A labels 13 Nov; (4) AA verification 15 Nov then fit and freeze 16 Nov, SIM-VAL 18 Nov; (5) D5 review 16 Nov, freeze, runs 17-18, results 19; (6) hard freeze 21 Nov, report and slides 21-24, rehearsal 24. 07.A cannot open 23b by 25 Nov (15b unfrozen), so it is lower value than D5 and AA; if the human week slips, cut 07.A first (report as FAILED-on-record), then SIM-VAL, never D5. Hosts: server runs are VPN dependent (vinayak GPU for LLM rungs); manjot lacks sklearn, hypothesis, lxml, torch, so installs need human authorisation and 29-diag must run on the Mac. Hour figures are estimates and agent-hour totals for report/slides (about 15-22 h) must begin before results exist.
